issues.legal_issue: Registration of an FIR is mandatory when the information prima facie discloses a cognizable offence, and a preliminary inquiry is not required in that situation.
A preliminary inquiry may be conducted only when the information does not disclose a cognizable offence but indicates that inquiry is necessary to determine whether one is disclosed.
Courts cannot issue a blanket direction requiring preliminary inquiries before future FIRs or restraining the registration of FIRs, as that would conflict with the statutory framework.
Allegations that successive FIRs were registered with an ulterior motive do not justify a blanket pre-FIR inquiry requirement and may be pursued through remedies available under law.
